snippet.title: WarDogs Devs on UE5 Performance: "Is That the Pen's Fault?"
snippet.description:
Back in March, before launch, a viewer asked in BULKHEAD's Q&A whether a 100-player game on a giant UE5 map needs a 5090 with frame gen to hit 60 FPS. Joe Brammer said they've thought about performance from day one: they asked a local PC shop for the standard gaming PC somebody's mum would buy their kid, put it under a desk in the studio, and made it their base spec. Tim on Unreal Engine games that run badly: easy access to the engine doesn't mean every game is well optimized. "Is that the pen's fault?"

snippet.title: EndSARS Memorial+Shettima’s Promise On Security+Wike Slams Atiku+Nigeria Confirms Ebola Case|OjyOkpe
snippet.description:
Police fired teargas at mourners, journalists and two Lagos governorship candidates at the Lekki Toll Gate during the sixth anniversary of the EndSARS protests.

Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour and Funso Doherty were among those affected as participants gathered to honour victims, including journalist Pelumi Onifade. Meanwhile, a new Foundation for Investigative Journalism report alleges that police extortion and brutality remain widespread six years after SARS was disbanded.

Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory after a woman who travelled from Uganda tested positive. Health authorities have identified 44 close contacts and begun contact tracing.

Uganda, however, says the woman transited through the country without symptoms after travelling to the Democratic Republic of Congo, stressing that the location of infection remains under investigation.

Vice President Kashim Shettima is facing renewed criticism over security in Northern Nigeria following an opinion article questioning the government's response to banditry, school closures and displacement.

The commentary also raises questions about federal relief allocations and the administration's security promises ahead of the 2027 elections.

FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has urged Rivers State youths to support President Bola Tinubu's re-election bid in 2027, while criticising former Vice President Atiku Abubakar as untrustworthy.

Separately, the APC Presidential Campaign Council has denied allegations of a plot to assassinate Atiku, demanding evidence from those making the claims and insisting that presidential candidates' security remains in place.

“It’s clear journalists have maybe gone over the line in trying to pursue their agenda.”

snippet.title: Why Is This Country Inside Another Country? 🌍 #geography #shorts #facts
snippet.description:
Why does a tiny country cut almost 500 km through another country? 🌍😳

Look at the map of Africa. Senegal is almost split by a narrow, snake-shaped country called The Gambia. But why does this bizarre border exist?

The answer takes us back to a fierce colonial rivalry between Britain and France.

In 1889, the two empires negotiated boundaries around the strategically important Gambia River, creating one of Africa's most unusual country shapes.

Discover how geography, colonial history, and a single river shaped the map of West Africa!

💬 What other strange borders should we explore next? Comment below!

Why does a thin strip of land cut through Senegal? Discover the history behind the unusual Senegal Gambia border. 🌍

The Gambia is essentially a long, narrow enclave surrounded by Senegal on three sides, with the Atlantic Ocean to the west. This strange layout is the result of colonial-era negotiations between Britain and France in 1889. The two powers drew borders based on the Gambia River, which served as a crucial trade route for the British at the time.

By tracing the river’s path, the colonial powers created one of the most distinct map anomalies in West Africa. Understanding how this border was formed offers a clear look at how historical trade interests continue to shape modern national boundaries. These geography facts highlight how colonial decisions still influence the world map today.

snippet.title: Russia’s Hidden FPV Drone Disguised as Autumn Leaves #ukraine #drone #russia #fpvdrone #russia #fpv
snippet.description:
A Russian FPV drone discovered by Ukrainian soldiers was reportedly camouflaged with dry autumn leaves and painted to blend into the roadside environment. Unlike conventional attack drones that chase targets, this is described as a “waiting drone,” designed to remain concealed on the ground until a vehicle approaches.

According to the claims, its motors can be switched off after landing, while its battery, electronics, propellers and fiber-optic spool are covered to reduce visibility. A fiber-optic control link can also make the drone less vulnerable to conventional radio-frequency jamming, although it does not make the device impossible to detect.

The discovery highlights a disturbing evolution in drone warfare. Drones are no longer just about speed, range or explosive payloads—they can also be designed to blend into their surroundings and wait for the right moment. On the frontline, the threat may not always come from the sky. Sometimes, it could be lying unnoticed right beside the road.

snippet.title: Australian lawmaker wounded in attack has lost both her legs, husband says | AFP
snippet.description:
Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has had both legs amputated after being hit by a car, her husband said, in what police described as a targeted attack. 
 
Haines is now in a stable condition after being struck by a car on 19 October near her office in the town of Wangaratta, just over 200 kilometres northeast of the Victoria state capital.
